risks.title: Same-supplier payments combining past the quote threshold
risks.statement: Payments to one supplier close together may be a single requirement split so each stays under the invitation-to-quote threshold [rule:CPR-13] [rule:CPR-60]. These are risk indicators to investigate, not findings.

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.split_purchases@25000.counts.flagged_items}} flagged supplier groups, of which {{$.tests.split_purchases@25000.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count}} are care or education placements and {{$.tests.split_purchases@25000.by_tag.grant.count}} grants, leaving well over twenty outside the exempt tags [metric:$.tests.split_purchases@25000.counts.flagged_items]; the combined total is far above the tier value of [rule:CPR-60]. Clustering just under the same threshold is below the L4 count, so L5 is not met [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering@25000.counts.flagged_items].

uplift.reason: The Contract Letting audit has a Reasonable opinion [history:AUD-01], so it is not a repeat finding.

impact.justification: General-procurement-tagged combined value of {{$.tests.split_purchases@25000.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp|gbp}} alone exceeds the top council impact band [metric:$.tests.split_purchases@25000.by_tag.general_procurement]; total combined {{$.tests.split_purchases@25000.totals_gbp.combined|gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases@25000.totals_gbp.combined].

risks.focus: Recommend testing the largest non-care groups for one underlying requirement, excluding equal-amount recurring care charges.

risks.title: Low-value payments clustering and combining at the lowest quote boundary
risks.statement: Many payments sit just under, or combine past, the lowest procurement-route boundary [rule:CPR-59], and the anti-splitting rule applies [rule:CPR-13]. Risk indicators to investigate.

likelihood.justification: Two independent tests meet L4 at this tier: {{$.tests.split_purchases@1000.counts.flagged_items}} split groups [metric:$.tests.split_purchases@1000.counts.flagged_items] and {{$.tests.threshold_clustering@1000.counts.flagged_items}} near-threshold payments [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering@1000.counts.flagged_items], each with well over twenty items outside the exempt tags, engaging [rule:CPR-59]. Much of the clustering is care-tagged, which may reflect tariff pricing.

uplift.reason: No adverse audit opinion on this theme [history:AUD-11].

impact.justification: General-procurement-tagged combined value {{$.tests.split_purchases@1000.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp|gbp}} falls in the Medium band [metric:$.tests.split_purchases@1000.by_tag.general_procurement]; the lower-value tier limits financial exposure per [rule:CPR-59].

risks.focus: Recommend a small targeted sample of non-care groups to confirm whether quotes were obtained; lower priority than the larger-tier split risk.

risks.title: Combined payments approaching the high-value approval and tender tier
risks.statement: Payments to one supplier combine past the high-value tier [rule:CPR-64] [rule:CPR-04], which carries enhanced approval. Risk indicators to investigate.

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.split_purchases@500000.counts.flagged_items}} flagged groups, with {{$.tests.split_purchases@500000.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count}} in the care tag, leaving between five and nineteen outside the exempt tags [metric:$.tests.split_purchases@500000.counts.flagged_items]; no payment clusters just under the tier [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering@500000.counts.flagged_items].

impact.justification: General-procurement-tagged combined value {{$.tests.split_purchases@500000.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp|gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases@500000.by_tag.general_procurement] engages the approval rule [rule:CPR-04].

risks.focus: Recommend confirming the approval route and any existing contract for the few non-care groups.

risks.title: Spend with suppliers having no council contract notice
risks.statement: Suppliers whose annualised estimate exceeds the notice threshold have no exact-name council notice [rule:CPR-61] [rule:CPR-14]. Many may hold frameworks or contracts not published as notices. Risk indicators to investigate.

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.flagged_items}} suppliers flagged, of which {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.count}} grants and {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count}} care placements are exempt tags, leaving well over twenty [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.flagged_items]; annualised estimate {{$.tests.off_contract.totals_gbp.annualised_estimate|gbp}} exceeds the tier of [rule:CPR-61]. The Contracts Finder export only holds larger contracts, which limits this test [metric:$.limitations]. [history:RT-01]

impact.justification: General-procurement-tagged three-month payments {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp|gbp}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement] exceed the top band; value for money is a registered theme [history:RT-03].

evidence: Suppliers with a near-miss candidate notice: {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.with_candidate_notice}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.with_candidate_notice]
risks.focus: Recommend requesting contract, framework or exclusion evidence for the largest non-care, non-grant suppliers, starting with near-miss name candidates.

risks.title: Payments after the only matching notice has ended
risks.statement: Suppliers paid in the window whose every matching notice ended earlier may indicate spend after expiry without an approved extension [rule:CPR-69]. A newer contract may exist without a notice. Risk indicators to investigate.

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.flagged_items}} suppliers flagged, none in exempt tags, which is between five and nineteen [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.flagged_items], engaging [rule:CPR-69].

impact.justification: Three-month payments {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.totals_gbp.three_month|gbp}} fall in the Medium band [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.totals_gbp.three_month].

risks.focus: Recommend requesting extension or new-contract records for each flagged supplier.

risks.title: Spend running above the awarded contract value
risks.statement: Annualised spend is well above the annual equivalent of the award, which may indicate spend beyond the award without an approved variation [rule:CPR-70] [rule:CPR-71]. Award values may be estimates. Risk indicators to investigate.

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.flagged_items}} suppliers flagged of {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.assessed}} assessed, none in exempt tags [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.flagged_items], engaging [rule:CPR-70].

impact.justification: Flagged annualised estimate {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.totals_gbp.annualised_estimate_flagged|gbp}} [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.totals_gbp.annualised_estimate_flagged], an annualised estimate of the spend at these suppliers, not of any overspend.

risks.focus: Recommend comparing payments with the award and any variation approvals for the flagged suppliers.

risks.title: Possible duplicate payments
risks.statement: Repeated same-amount payments to one supplier within a short window may be duplicates to investigate; identical rows may be legitimate. Financial control is a registered theme [history:RT-02].

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.duplicates.counts.flagged_items}} flagged items [metric:$.tests.duplicates.counts.flagged_items], but no Contract Procedure Rule directly addresses duplicate payments, so L3 and L4 conditions are not met; the Accounts Payable audit was Reasonable [history:AUD-11]. Lower level taken.

uplift.reason: Reasonable opinion is not a repeat finding [history:AUD-11].

risks.focus: Recommend a lower-priority sample of non-care identical groups against invoices.
